title: Noteman Production Directory Tree & Storage Architecture
description: Defines the production filesystem hierarchy and file placement rules inspired by Linux Package Managers (FHS / XDG). Specific file types and roles are strictly partitioned into dedicated directories to maintain referential integrity and prevent orphaned assets.

db/.purpose: State and relational metadata storage (analogous to /var/lib in Linux).

contents.noteman.db: Active SQLite database storing subjects, threads, files, tasks, and indexes.
contents.noteman.db-wal: SQLite write-ahead log for high concurrency and atomic commits.
contents.noteman.db-shm: SQLite shared memory index for WAL.

backups/.purpose: Automatic and manual database snapshots / backups.

notes/.purpose: User-authored notes and source documents created via embedded editors (is_material = 0).

markdown/.purpose: Dedicated storage for Markdown notes and outlines.

latex/.purpose: Dedicated storage for LaTeX source files, math documents, and bibliography files.

misc/.purpose: Plain text notes, snippets, or code snippets authored by the user.

materials/.purpose: Imported academic course materials, external documents, and references (is_material = 1).

pdf/.purpose: Course textbooks, lecture slide PDFs, syllabus, and examination papers.

docs/.purpose: External office documents and reference specifications.

archives/.purpose: Compressed code packages, dataset archives, and lab source archives.

media/.purpose: Embedded multimedia assets referenced within notes (images, graphs, audio).

images/.purpose: Diagrams, screenshots, whiteboard captures, and figures embedded in Markdown or LaTeX.

audio/.purpose: Lecture voice recordings or audio explanations.

cache/.purpose: Ephemeral build artifacts, math formula rendering cache, and staged exports (analogous to /var/cache).
cache/.lifecycle: Ephemeral, purgeable without loss of persistent data

katex/.purpose: Cached rendered KaTeX math expressions / SVG glyph cache for fast editor previews.

previews/.purpose: Generated thumbnail previews and rendered page representations of PDFs and LaTeX docs.

latex_builds/.purpose: Intermediate compilation artifacts (.aux, .log, .out, .toc, .synctex) produced by tectonic/pdflatex engines.

exports/.purpose: Staged exports (HTML / PDF) generated on demand before the user saves them to an external location.

config/.purpose: User configurations, editor presets, and customizable templates (analogous to /etc).

subdirectories.settings.json: App preferences (theme, font, KaTeX macros, auto-save interval, default semester).

templates/markdown/.purpose: Starter Markdown templates for lectures, lab reports, and revision summaries.

templates/latex/.purpose: Starter LaTeX templates for homework submissions, research papers, and cheat sheets.

logs/.purpose: Diagnostics, runtime logs, crash traces, and database migration audit logs (analogous to /var/log).

contents.integrity.log: Audit trail of database-to-filesystem verification runs.

package_manager_principles.strict_type_routing: Every file imported or authored must be routed to its strictly assigned subdirectory according to its file_type and is_material flag.
package_manager_principles.atomic_file_ops: Writing the file payload to disk and inserting its metadata into SQLite must be coordinated. If disk write fails, no DB record is created; if DB insert fails, the uncommitted file is cleaned up.
package_manager_principles.clean_uninstallation: Deleting a file, thread, or subject removes both SQLite records and physical files on disk to prevent orphaned files.
package_manager_principles.integrity_verification: The system includes an integrity verification command (verify_files_integrity) like 'pacman -Qk' to check that each database record corresponds to a verified file on disk.
package_manager_principles.safe_cache_purge: The entire cache/ directory can be purged at any time without compromising database consistency or user documents.
